name: ecl
why: Embeddable Common Lisp is an old-school, unusual implementation with a real compiler and a strange lineage worth exploring.

brief.what_it_is: ECL (Embeddable Common-Lisp) is a Common Lisp implementation. The project's GitLab page describes it as the "Embeddable Common-Lisp main repository" and lists the license as GNU LGPLv2.1. The homepage I reached is a news and release blog, so I could not confirm from the fetched pages what it takes in or what it produces. The brew description and executables suggest an interpreter and compiler binary (ecl) plus a config helper (ecl-config).
brief.why_it_exists: The fetched pages do not state the motivation. The name suggests a Common Lisp meant to be embedded in other programs, but I did not find the author's own framing of that.
brief.install_notes: No installation steps were visible in the pages I could read. The GitLab README body loaded empty, and the manual link returned 404. Brew lists two executables: ecl and ecl-config.
brief.standout: The project has a long history: the homepage blog runs from 2005 to 2026, with releases such as 26.5.5 on 2026-05-05 and 26.3.27 on 2026-03-27. That suggests a long-running, old-school implementation, though I could not verify the compiler or lineage claims from the brief.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage's most recent post is the ECL 26.5.5 release dated 2026-05-05, and the page was last modified on 2026-05-05. Earlier releases are 26.3.27 (2026-03-27) and 24.5.10 (2024-05-10), so releases are spaced irregularly.
brief.caveats: I could not reach the README text or the manual, so commands, install steps, platform support and features are unverified. The scout note's claims of a real compiler and unusual lineage are unconfirmed by anything I read. The homepage has no project description beyond its title, so the writer should not treat the blog index as documentation.

judge.reason: ECL makes Common Lisp embeddable in C programs and compiles Lisp through C, offering a distinctive way to explore both a language and its implementation.

entry.title: ECL
entry.tldr: A maintained Common Lisp implementation built to be embedded in other programs, with a REPL and a small config helper.
entry.deeper_look:
ECL is short for Embeddable Common-Lisp. The project's GitLab page calls it the "Embeddable Common-Lisp main repository" and lists the license as GNU LGPLv2.1. Brew installs two executables: `ecl`, the Lisp implementation itself, and `ecl-config`, which by its name reports configuration details for building against it.

The name points to the idea underneath it. Common Lisp is a large, old, standardized language, and an implementation meant to be embedded suggests a Lisp you can put inside another program instead of only running it on its own. The pages I could read do not spell out how that works, so treat the specifics as something to find out by poking at it.

The project is not new. Its release blog runs from 2005 to 2026, with recent releases 26.3.27 and 26.5.5. For a reader curious about Lisp, that makes it a long-running alternative to the better-known implementations, and a way into a language family with a very different feel from most modern tools.

Shows what the configuration helper can report.

entry.whats_unique: It is a Common Lisp that is named for, and aimed at, being embedded in other software. It also has a release history of roughly twenty years.
entry.caveats: The README and manual were not reachable when this was written, so specific features, platform support and usage are unverified; the homepage is only a release blog.
